findings.forcedInvention: The rest of every truncated sentence: what happens to a co-presence edge published before its credit publishes; what state 02 holds a 05 delivery-acceptance credit CLAIM in; what the release event does to embargo; what happens to a live credit when a venue record is merged/retired. findings.claim: 11 of the 25 `## 3. High-Confidence Synthesis` blocks in ideation-cx.md are hard-truncated mid-word / mid-clause, and the cut content exists nowhere else in the tree.
findings.evidence: ideation-cx.md — ten `- **Synthesis**:` lines are exactly 817 characters long and one is exactly 1313, each ending mid-token: line 350 (02-03) ends "…Constraint: a co-presence edge published before its credit publishes routes around embar"; line 362 (02-05) ends "…05's delivery-acceptance commit emits a credit CLAIM (not a fact) that 02 carries as unatteste"; line 380 (02-08) ends "…two independent close prompts (08.05.04 vs 02.02.03) fire at the same instant — probable merge. Near-col"; line 404 (02-12) ends "…Trigger: the release event authoritatively lifts embar"; line 422 (02-16) ends "…relocation makes a moved venue a DIFFERENT record (D-04) and merge retires an identifier — a live". Same defect at lines 356, 368, 374, 386, 392, 398. Complete blocks for comparison: line 410 (len 660) and line 416 (len 813) both end with a full stop. The file nonetheless declares "**Status**: [DEEP]" (ideation-cx.md:5) and "Last updated: 2026-07-29" (:6). The lost text is NOT recoverable: `grep -r` over the whole ideation tree for "merge retires an identifier", "co-presence edge published before its credit", "carries as unatteste" and "Near-col" returns ideation-cx.md and nothing else; the linked source-domain file 02-credits-attribution/credits-attribution-cx.md contains none of these phrases. ideation-cx.md is the only file in the tree with more than one 817-character line (10 of them).
findings.failureScenario: An implementer specifying the Credits↔Venues interaction reads ideation-cx.md:422, reaches "merge retires an identifier — a live", and has no statement of what happens to a live credit citing a merged venue record. Following the documented escape hatch ("Full detail lives in the source-domain CX file linked in §2", ideation-cx.md:272) leads to credits-attribution-cx.md, which does not contain the rule either. The same dead end repeats for the 02-03 embargo constraint, the 02-05 claim-state rule, the 02-08 duplicate-close-prompt race, the 02-11 shared-verification-mechanism candidate and the 02-12 embargo-lift trigger. Two implementers invent two different answers, and the CX file cannot be used to detect the divergence.

findings.forcedInvention: The CX-M number → mechanism mapping. The implementer must invent (or reverse-engineer by counting unnumbered table rows) which mechanism each of CX-M01…CX-M32 names, and must decide which of the two candidate tables the numbering indexes.
findings.claim: The `CX-M##` cross-cut mechanism identifier space — referenced 830 times across 132 ideation files, including inside the root files themselves — is defined in no file, and the two candidate tables give conflicting answers for the same identifier.
findings.evidence: Root files reference the ids without a legend: ideation-cx.md:262 "shares the CX-M14 shipping cross-cut and nothing else"; ideation-cx.md:250 "really a Safeguarding cross-cut (CX-M31) touching both domains"; moscow-ledger.md:745 "strains CX-M01's escrow model (months-long holds…)". But the file that declares itself "the super-CX holding the mechanism registry" (ideation-cx.md:3) publishes a 25-row table whose columns are `| Mechanism | Owner | Serves | Definition | Key constraints |` (ideation-cx.md:15) with NO id column — and only 25 rows, so `CX-M31` has no referent at all, while row 14 of that table is "Localization, Currency & Timezone" (ideation-cx.md:30), not Shipping. The numbering actually indexes the 32-row `## Cross-cutting systems` table in domain-map-proposal.md:340-373, which is also unnumbered: counting rows there gives 1 Payments (= CX-M01 escrow ✓), 14 "Shipping, Fulfilment & Logistics" (domain-map-proposal.md:355, = CX-M14 shipping ✓), 31 "Safeguarding & Minor Protection" (:372, = CX-M31 ✓), 7 Notifications, 8 Reviews, 19 Audit Log — all matching live usages (`CX-M07 Notifications & Alerts`, `CX-M08 Reviews`, `CX-M19 Audit Log & Provenance Ledger`, and 13-gear-marketplace/gear-marketplace-cx.md:388-390 "**CX-M04** Atomic Payment ↔ Rights Transfer … **CX-M31** Safeguarding & Minor Protection … **CX-M11** Real-Time Rooms"). No file in the repository binds a CX-M number to a name: `grep -rn "^| *\*\*\?CX-M"` over the tree returns only prose references, the maximum number of distinct CX-M ids in any single file is 17, and the historical docs/wejammin-domain-map-proposal.md table (line 822) is likewise unnumbered.
findings.failureScenario: A downstream workflow (or human) resolving "CX-M14" in ideation-cx.md:262 opens the registry the index calls authoritative (ideation-index.md:74 "Cross-cut mechanisms (consolidated registry) | **25** — in `ideation-cx.md`"), counts to row 14, and gets Localization, Currency & Timezone — the wrong mechanism, silently. Resolving "CX-M31" against the same 25-row table yields nothing and looks like a typo. The correct answer is only obtainable by guessing that an unnumbered table in a different file, described as a recovery proposal, defines the id space.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether 8 named cross-cutting systems still exist, who owns them, and what their constraints are — or whether each consuming domain should build its own.
findings.claim: Eight of the 32 ratified cross-cutting systems in domain-map-proposal.md have no row in the 25-mechanism registry ideation-cx.md presents as the consolidated one, and no root file records them as merged, renamed, dropped or deferred.
findings.evidence: Present in domain-map-proposal.md `## Cross-cutting systems` (:340-373) and absent from the ideation-cx.md §1 registry (:15-41): "Atomic Payment ↔ Rights Transfer" (:345), "DAW & Desktop Bridge" (:353), "Onboarding & Role-Aware Activation" (:356), "Accessibility" (:362), "Promoted Placement & Advertising" (:366), "Referrals, Invites & Affiliates" (:367), "Follow, Save & Watchlist" (:369), "Offline & Low-Connectivity Field Resilience" (:373). Seven of the eight are still referenced by live id from feature and CX files — CX-M04 ×21, CX-M15 ×19, CX-M21 ×7, CX-M25 ×10, CX-M28 ×22, CX-M32 ×12, CX-M12 ×2 references — and by name, e.g. 06-education-lessons-mentorship/education-lessons-mentorship-cx.md:406 "**Onboarding & Role-Aware Activation** | Enabling the teaching facet", :408 "**Promoted Placement & Advertising** | Teacher/course placement | **Values-laden in a minors-facing market** (06.02 Q-02) — unresolved", :410 "**Referrals, Invites & Affiliates**", :411 "**Follow, Save & Watchlist** | Saving teachers/courses". The index counts both inventories without reconciling them: ideation-index.md:202 (D-16) "24 domains, 423 candidate sub-domains, **32 cross-cuts**" vs ideation-index.md:74 "Cross-cut mechanisms (consolidated registry) | **25**". The registry's own §1b states the exact hazard: "Downstream (`/create-prd`) MUST rule on promotion before any owning domain builds a private copy — the failure mode is each domain rebuilding a subtly incompatible version" (ideation-cx.md:45) — yet that warning is attached only to 2 candidates, not to these 8.
findings.failureScenario: Domain 06's CX file tells an implementer that "Follow, Save & Watchlist" and "Promoted Placement & Advertising" are cross-cuts serving education; the global registry — the file the index designates as the mechanism registry — has no row for either, so there is no owner, definition or key-constraint set to build against. Domains 03, 04, 06, 13, 14, 16, 20 each implement their own watchlist/save primitive with different semantics, which is the failure mode ideation-cx.md:45 exists to prevent.

findings.claim: domain-map-proposal.md lists "band" (and ~40 other role names) under **Personas** for nine domains, directly contradicting D-19's statement that Band is an entity and not a persona, and the index's claim of zero personas outside the four.
findings.evidence: domain-map-proposal.md:60 "**Personas.** Working musician; band; manager; agent; studio owner; venue operator; label; dealer/shop."; also :84, :144, :240, :252, :264, :288 all list "band" under **Personas** (9 Persona lines mention band or band treasurer). The contradicting statements, both in ideation-index.md: :205 (D-19) "**4 primary personas**: `Musician` … `Producer` … `Operator` … `Fan` (per D-11). **Band is an entity (domain 01), not a persona.**" and :70 "| Invented personas | **0** — only Musician / Producer / Operator / Fan |". ideation-cx.md:283 restates the rule in the CX prose — "the Band is an entity (not a persona), so board exclusion and alerts must be entity-membership-aware" — so the tree elsewhere treats this as a load-bearing distinction, not loose wording.
